Maintenance Report — MNT-0152-008

Asset: WELL-0152 (NE-08 Well 152, T200, Northeast Block 8) Equipment: flowline Work started: 03 Mar 2024 08:00 · Finished: 13 Mar 2024 22:00 · Well stopped for this job: 254 hours Crew lead: Daniel Foster (U-302) · Crew: Brian Coleman · Contractor: Tumbleweed Flowline Co. Triggered by: inspection INS-0152-0072 on 2024-02-29 Report written: 19 Mar 2024

What happened

Field staff reported that a damp, dark patch appeared along the flowline route. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0152-0072 showed the wellhead at 14.9 °C with the air at 15.9 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. Excavation found a corrosion pinhole on the bottom of the line. The well stayed shut in for about 9 days longer than the repair itself because the job had to wait for a weekday contractor slot.

Root cause

External corrosion where the pipe coating had been damaged.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 5 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).
  • Hot work permit issued for welding; gas test before welding read 2% LEL, below the 10% limit (WS-04).

Work done

  1. Excavated around the leak.
  2. Cut out the corroded section.
  3. Welded in a new section of line pipe.
  4. Coated the new joint.
  5. Backfilled after the pressure test.

Summary of the fix: cut out and replaced the corroded flowline section.

Testing and return to service

Pressure-tested the repaired section at 276 psi (1.25 × the flowline's maximum operating pressure of 221 psi) and held it for 4 hours with no pressure drop (WS-05). The well was returned to production.

Waste

  • Oily soil from the excavation and the cut-out pipe sent to an approved disposal site under waste manifest WM-0152-008 (WS-06).

maintenance.report_html:
Maintenance Report — MNT-0152-015

Asset: WELL-0152 (NE-08 Well 152, T200, Northeast Block 8) Equipment: flowline Work started: 31 Jan 2025 08:00 · Finished: 01 Feb 2025 00:00 · Well stopped for this job: 16 hours Crew lead: Daniel Foster (U-302) · Crew: Brian Coleman, Megan Ward Triggered by: inspection INS-0152-0120 on 2025-01-30 Report written: 01 Feb 2025

What happened

The weekly drone inspection INS-0152-0120 at 08:00 on 2025-01-30 found crude oil on the pad: about 3.3% of the pad area, estimated 1.0 bbl. The inspector noted: "Pooled fluid near flowline." The field operator shut the well in, closed the flowline valve and placed earth berms and absorbent pads. The release was contained about 3.1 hours after the inspection. The crew traced the leak to a threaded coupling on the flowline close to the wellhead.

Root cause

Corrosion under a failed protective wrap on the coupling. This is corrective repair number 3 on this well's flowline in the last 12 months.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 0 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).
  • Hot work permit issued for welding; gas test before welding read 0% LEL, below the 10% limit (WS-04).

Work done

  1. Excavated around the coupling.
  2. Cut out the failed coupling and the pipe ends.
  3. Welded in new pipe and a new fitting.
  4. Coated the new joints.
  5. Excavated the stained soil.
  6. Backfilled after the pressure test.

Summary of the fix: replaced leaking flowline section and remediated soil.

Testing and return to service

Pressure-tested the repaired section at 276 psi (1.25 × the flowline's maximum operating pressure of 221 psi) and held it for 4 hours with no pressure drop (WS-05). The well was returned to production.

Spill clean-up and waste

  • About 1.2 m³ of stained soil excavated, bagged and sent to an approved disposal site under waste manifest WM-0152-015 (WS-06).
  • 2 soil samples taken around the spill; the highest result after clean-up was 0.26% TPH, below the 1.0% target (SR-03).

Total10,512

Notes and recommendations

  • Inspect the remaining joints on this flowline.
  • Record the leak location for the flowline maintenance program (RC-05).
  • Start a root-cause analysis for this equipment before the next repair is closed (well-type manual, section 10).
